title: Creating and rotating API keys
text: API keys authenticate server-to-server calls. Create a key under Settings > Access, give it the narrowest scope that works, and store it in your secret manager. To rotate a key without downtime, create the replacement first, deploy it, then revoke the old key; revoked keys stop working within 60 seconds.

title: Single sign-on with SAML
text: Enterprise workspaces can require SAML single sign-on through Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or any SAML 2.0 identity provider. Upload the IdP metadata XML, map the email attribute, and test with one admin before enforcing login through SSO for everyone.

title: Provisioning users with SCIM
text: SCIM 2.0 keeps users and groups in sync with your identity provider. When an employee leaves the company and is deactivated in the IdP, their sessions are revoked, their access is removed and their seat is freed on the next sync.

title: Roles and permissions
text: Workspaces have four built-in roles: Owner, Admin, Developer and Viewer. Custom roles combine individual permissions, for example letting a contractor deploy services without seeing billing or invoices.

title: Two-factor authentication
text: Owners can require two-factor authentication for every member. Supported methods are authenticator apps and hardware security keys using WebAuthn; SMS codes are not offered because they can be intercepted.

title: Audit log
text: The audit log records who changed what and when: sign-ins, role changes, API key creation and deletion, and configuration edits. Entries are kept for one year and can be streamed to your SIEM.

title: Invoices and billing history
text: Invoices are issued on the first day of each month and emailed to the billing contact. Download past invoices as PDF from Billing > History; each invoice lists usage by project.

title: Payment methods
text: Pay by credit card or, on annual plans, by bank transfer against an invoice. If a card payment fails we retry the charge three times over seven days before the workspace is suspended.

title: How usage is priced
text: Compute is billed per vCPU-second and memory per GiB-second while services are running. Storage is billed per GiB-month and outbound data transfer per GiB; inbound traffic is free and never charged.

title: Budgets and spending alerts
text: Set a monthly budget per project and get email or webhook alerts at 50, 80 and 100 percent of spend. A hard limit can pause non-production services so you never overspend the budget.

title: Refunds and credits
text: Service credits are issued automatically when monthly uptime falls below the SLA. For billing mistakes such as a duplicate charge, open a ticket within 30 days of the invoice date and we refund the money to the original payment method.

title: Regions and availability zones
text: You can deploy services to us-east, us-west, eu-central and ap-south. Each region has three availability zones; production services should run in at least two zones so a zone outage does not take them down.

title: Automatic database backups
text: Managed databases take a full snapshot every night and stream write-ahead logs continuously, which allows point-in-time recovery to any second in the last 14 days. Snapshots are encrypted and stored in a second region.

title: Restoring a database
text: To recover from an accidental delete or a dropped table, restore to a new database instance at a timestamp just before the mistake, verify the data, then switch your application's connection string. Restores never overwrite the original instance.

title: Data retention
text: Application logs are kept for 30 days, metrics for 13 months and audit log entries for one year. Deleted projects are recoverable for 7 days, after which all of their data is permanently erased.

title: Exporting and deleting personal data
text: To answer a GDPR or CCPA request from a customer, export everything stored about a person as JSON from the Privacy page, or delete it; deletion completes within 30 days, including backups.

title: API rate limits
text: The public API allows 600 requests per minute per key. When you exceed the limit you get HTTP 429 Too Many Requests errors with a Retry-After header, so back off and retry after that many seconds.

title: Webhooks
text: Webhooks notify your endpoint about deploys, incidents and billing events. Each delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the Acme-Signature header; verify the signature with your signing secret to confirm the request really came from us.

title: Webhook delivery and retries
text: Deliveries that do not get a 2xx response within 10 seconds are retried with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours. Make your handler idempotent using the event id, because the same event can be received twice.

title: Client libraries
text: Official SDKs exist for Java, Python, Go and TypeScript. They handle authentication, pagination and automatic retries on 429 and 5xx errors; pin a version and upgrade deliberately.

title: Installing the acme CLI
text: Install the command-line tool on a Mac with Homebrew (brew install acme), with Scoop on Windows, or download a binary for Linux. Run acme login once to authenticate, then acme deploy from your project directory.

title: Kubernetes operator
text: The operator lets you manage databases and queues as Kubernetes custom resources. Install it with Helm, then declare an AcmeDatabase object; the operator provisions it and writes the credentials into a Secret.

title: Autoscaling services
text: Services scale horizontally between a minimum and maximum instance count based on CPU, memory or requests per second. Scale to zero when idle is available for staging and other non-production services and adds a cold start of a few seconds.

title: Metrics and dashboards
text: Every service exports CPU, memory, request rate, error rate and latency percentiles. Dashboards are built in, and Grafana or any Prometheus-compatible tool can read the same metrics from the scrape endpoint.

title: Alerting
text: Create alert rules on any metric, for example p95 latency above 500 ms for five minutes. Notifications go to email, Slack, PagerDuty or a webhook, and alerts resolve automatically when the condition clears.

title: Status page and incidents
text: Platform incidents are posted on the status page with updates at least every 30 minutes. Subscribe by email or RSS, or receive incident webhooks to open tickets in your own tracker.

title: Uptime SLA
text: Production plans include a 99.95 percent monthly uptime guarantee for services deployed in two or more availability zones. If we miss it, you receive service credits of 10 to 30 percent of the monthly bill.

title: Support plans
text: Standard support answers tickets within one business day. Premium support adds a 1-hour response time for production outages, a named technical account manager and quarterly architecture reviews.

title: Maintenance windows
text: Minor version upgrades of managed Postgres and MySQL are applied during a weekly maintenance window you choose. Major version upgrades are never automatic; you schedule them and can test on a cloned instance first.

title: Private networking
text: Connect services to your own VPC with peering or a private endpoint so traffic never crosses the public internet. Peering is supported with AWS, Azure and Google Cloud networks.

title: Encryption
text: Data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or later. Enterprise workspaces can bring their own encryption key from AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault and revoke it to make the data unreadable.

title: Environment variables and secrets
text: Store configuration such as database passwords as environment variables per environment. Values marked secret are encrypted, hidden in the dashboard and logs, and only injected into running services; changing one triggers a rolling restart.

title: Exporting logs
text: Ship application and audit logs to Datadog, Splunk, an S3 bucket or any HTTPS endpoint. Log drains batch entries every few seconds and retry when the destination is down.

title: Custom domains and TLS certificates
text: Point a CNAME record at your service and add your own domain in Settings; HTTPS certificates are issued and renewed automatically through Let's Encrypt. Wildcard domains need a DNS TXT record for verification.
